terms.sub: Resting Membrane Potential and Ionic Basis
clues: In large mammalian nerve fibers, it typically measures between -70 and -90 millivolts
It is governed primarily by background leak potassium channels and maintained long-term by the Na+/K+-ATPase pump
It is the steady electrical voltage difference across the plasma membrane of an unstimulated excitable cell

terms.sub: Resting Membrane Potential and Ionic Basis
clues: At 37 degrees Celsius, it uses the constant 61.5 divided by ion valence times the base-10 logarithm of the concentration ratio
Unlike the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz formula, it considers only one permeant ion species at a time
It calculates the exact equilibrium electrical potential that balances a single ion's chemical concentration gradient

terms.sub: Resting Membrane Potential and Ionic Basis
clues: It weights each monovalent ion's concentration gradient by its relative membrane permeability
Potassium dominates its output at rest because PK is roughly 50 to 100 times larger than PNa
It calculates the actual membrane potential when Na+, K+, and Cl- are simultaneously permeant
Graded receptor and synaptic potentials do not obey this rule
It explains why stimulus intensity must be encoded by firing frequency rather than spike height
Once depolarization reaches threshold, a full-amplitude stereotyped action potential fires regardless of further stimulus strength
In most mammalian neurons, it sits around -55 millivolts
Hypocalcemia shifts it closer to resting membrane potential, causing tetany
It is the critical membrane voltage where inward Na+ influx exceeds outward K+ efflux to trigger a regenerative spike
It prevents retrograde backward propagation and sets the maximum firing frequency of an axon
In ventricular cardiac muscle, the Phase 2 plateau prolongs it to ~200 milliseconds to prevent tetanus
During this window, no stimulus of any strength can elicit a second action potential because voltage-gated Na+ channels are inactivated
It coincides largely with late repolarization and the after-hyperpolarization undershoot
A second action potential triggered during this phase has a smaller peak amplitude
During this period, only a suprathreshold stimulus can evoke another spike because some Na+ channels have recovered while K+ conductance remains high
It occurs when a depolarizing current rises very slowly rather than abruptly
Voltage-gated Na+ inactivation (h) gates close and K+ channels open gradually before threshold firing can occur
This phenomenon explains why a slow ramp stimulus fails to trigger an action potential even after passing normal threshold voltage

terms.sub: Action Potential Propagation and Cable Properties
clues: It is also referred to as the initial segment of the axon
Summated EPSPs and IPSPs from the soma and dendrites converge here
It serves as the spike trigger zone of a neuron because it has the highest density of voltage-gated Na+ channels

terms.sub: Action Potential Propagation and Cable Properties
clues: It equals the square root of transverse membrane resistance divided by internal axial resistance
Both myelination and larger axon diameter increase this cable parameter
It is the distance over which a passive electrotonic potential decays to 37 percent (1/e) of its original amplitude
Its name comes from the Latin word meaning 'to leap' or 'to jump'
It conserves metabolic ATP energy by restricting transmembrane Na+ and K+ fluxes to unmyelinated gaps
Action potentials jump rapidly from one node of Ranvier to the next along myelinated axons
It is shorter in large fast myelinated axons and markedly prolonged in denervated muscle
It is measured directly from an excitable tissue's strength-duration curve
It is the minimum stimulus duration needed to excite a tissue using a current of twice rheobase strength

terms.sub: Voltage-Gated Ion Channels and Action Potential Phases
clues: It is a potent marine neurotoxin found in pufferfish (fugu) ovaries and liver
Unlike local anesthetics, it binds the outer pore mouth of the channel rather than the intracellular gate
It selectively blocks fast voltage-gated Na+ channels, abolishing Phase 0 depolarization in nerves and skeletal muscle

terms.sub: Motor Units, Summation, and Muscle Fiber Types
clues: It relies on Ohm's law because smaller neuron cell bodies have higher input resistance
It ensures that fatigue-resistant slow oxidative fibers are activated first during gentle movements
It states that alpha motor neurons are recruited in orderly progression from smallest to largest as force demand rises
It allows vascular arterioles and tonic sphincters to maintain pressure for hours without fatigue
It occurs when myosin light-chain phosphatase dephosphorylates myosin heads while they remain attached to actin
This smooth muscle state sustains tonic contractile tension with extremely low ATP consumption
